summary: Label–value pairs as a real `<dl>` — a record's details, a settings summary, a wizard's review step. Three layouts; an empty value is shown as "—" and read as words.
useWhen: showing a record's details as named values — Owner, Team, Last run
summarising what was entered before it is submitted — a wizard's review step
a strip of facts under a heading or on a card

useInstead.when: several records share the same fields and are compared down a column
useInstead.why: a table is for comparing rows; a description list is one record's values
a description list is read-only; an editable value is a field with a label, not a term
a stat leads with the number at display size; a description list reads label first, at body size

horizontal.use: the default — a record's details, the term beside its value. Stacks when the list itself is narrower than 24rem

stacked.use: a narrow column — a SidePanel, a card's side — term above value

row.use: a strip of short facts under a heading or in a card: pairs side by side at their own width, wrapping when out of room

requires: DescriptionListItem children only — each renders a `<div>` holding one `<dt>` and one `<dd>`
`emptyText` in the user's language when the page is not in English
guarantees: a `<dl>` of `<dt>` terms and `<dd>` definitions, so each value is read with its term and the list with its count
an empty value — null, undefined, false or '' — is drawn as "—" hidden from assistive technology and read as `emptyText` ("Not set")
0 is a value, not an empty one
`horizontal` stacks by the list's own width (a container query), so one list is right in a page and in a 22rem panel
long values — IDs, URLs — wrap inside their column rather than overflowing it
horizontal fills its parent's width; stacked and row size to their content, and none collapses in a shrink-to-fit parent such as a card's side column
notes: a value can be any content — a Badge, a Link, an Avatar with a name. Keep it to one value per term; several values are one `<dd>` holding a list
the term is text/secondary and the value text/default, so the eye lands on the value

antiPatterns.dont: a grid of <div>s with a label and a value in each
antiPatterns.why: divs say nothing: "Owner" and "Priya Shah" are read as two unrelated lines

antiPatterns.dont: a two-column <table> of labels and values
antiPatterns.why: a table announces rows and columns and invites comparing down a column; there is nothing to compare

antiPatterns.do: <DescriptionListItem term="Last run">{lastRun}</DescriptionListItem> — pass null when there is none
antiPatterns.why: a typed dash is read as "dash" or skipped; an empty value is read as "Not set"
